name: Glycogen Storage Disease Due to Glycogen Branching Enzyme Deficiency, Congenital Neuromuscular Form
aliases: Glycogen Storage Disease Type IV, Congenital Neuromuscular Variant

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Glycogen Storage Disease Type IV Neuromuscular Form

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient glycogen branching enzyme activity in muscle or liver biopsy
Congenital onset of hypotonia and muscle weakness with progressive neuromuscular symptoms
Identification of pathogenic variants in the GBE1 gene
Presence of abnormal glycogen deposits with fewer branch points in muscle or liver tissue

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Deficient glycogen branching enzyme activity plus clinical presentation consistent with congenital neuromuscular involvement and/or pathogenic GBE1 variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Muscle biopsy and genetic testing are critical for confirmation; clinical presentation alone is insufficient.

searchTerms: congenital muscle weakness with poor tone

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal glycogen structure with reduced branching detected in biopsy
searchTerms: abnormal glycogen with less branching in biopsy
glycogen structure defects seen in tissue sample
reduced glycogen branching detected in biopsy

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
searchTerms: respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
difficulty breathing caused by muscle weakness

laboratory: Reduced glycogen branching enzyme activity in muscle or liver tissue
Normal to mildly elevated liver transaminases
imaging: Muscle MRI showing fatty infiltration and muscle atrophy
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating abnormal glycogen with fewer branch points

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of glycogen branching enzyme deficiency

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness in infancy
Severe congenital hypotonia with feeding difficulties
Evidence of abnormal glycogen structure on biopsy
